title: What is still missing?
description: Conceptual projection of claim slices: supplying a fact versus supplying behavior, and extra work versus changed semantics. Neither axis is measured; regions overlap. General agent evidence admission is not implemented. Bind a fact means inspect and bind an existing behavior claim; implement behavior includes building or enforcing the missing consumer action.

tl.name: Inspectors
tl.description: An existing validator, codec, or transaction participant has the required behavior; the remaining question is whether inspection establishes the exact law. If the behavior is absent, this claim moves right.

tr.name: Conductors
tr.description: Checks, authority, or events must actually occur at the required point. Knowing a write set does not make a queued job finish. Policy remains authored; no mutation queue is implied.

bl.name: Surveyors
bl.description: Complete dependency inventories let an existing conservative consumer save irrelevant work. The current skipped-call gap strains this region: SQL-only known dependencies are not a complete footprint.

br.name: Machinists
br.description: Knowing query meaning or declared requirements still leaves executable coalescing or lowering machinery to build. This is the optimization slice, not all semantics of the source framework.

examples.label: F07 Installed validator
examples.plotReason: Prototype: inspect existing behavior whose truth controls accepted values.
examples.note: Placement assumes a real validator is installed. An unchecked cast belongs to a missing-behavior case.

examples.label: F06 Existing tx participant
examples.plotReason: Boundary case: inspection can establish use of an existing transaction.
examples.note: All relevant effects must use the supplied handle and finish before return. An escaping handle moves the claim right.

examples.label: F05 Job acknowledged early
examples.plotReason: Prototype: a correct footprint cannot create a later completion boundary.
examples.note: A preexisting wait-for-completion contract could make part of the remaining task inspectable.

examples.label: F11 Missing authored check
examples.plotReason: Tests that knowing policy coverage does not implement an absent check.
examples.note: Plots the missing-enforcement transfer slice, inferred from source contracts. Existing checks move left. Auth must remain authored.

examples.label: F03 Conditional footprint
examples.plotReason: Prototype: a broad complete bound can save reads without exact branch precision.
examples.note: Assumes settled relevant effects and a conservative consumer. General agent evidence admission is still absent.

examples.label: F02 Skipped opaque calls
examples.plotReason: Outlier: a partial producer result breaks the conservative-fallback premise.
examples.note: Just above the semantic watershed: current analysis records skipped calls while returning recognized SQL dependencies. Its partial footprint can change correctness, not merely read cost. It remains an outlier from the dependency-inventory cluster.

examples.label: F09 Fragment coalescing
examples.plotReason: Prototype: declaration knowledge still needs query construction machinery.
examples.note: Plots coalescing only. Masking and declaration provenance have semantic obligations above the line.

examples.label: F10 Predicate lowering
examples.plotReason: Separate mechanism: understanding an opaque predicate does not implement SQL lowering.
examples.note: Historical Links example; not a claim about current Links or an implemented Endpoints feature.

calibration.axisClaimType: Conceptual inference from typed source claims, constructed cases, and two code observations; coordinates are editorial, not measured.
calibration.secondAxisConfidence: Moderate. Extra-work placement requires an actual correct fallback; F02 is a counterpressure. Same fresh agent produced both maps, so they are internally correlated.
calibration.orthogonality: Useful four-region contrast: inspectable semantic facts and missing optimization machinery occupy both off-diagonal regions. A usable fact always presumes a consumer; missing admission machinery is not hidden by the left pole.
